newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian domestic credits 3.0 pct up in August.
newsitem.headline: Romanian domestic credits 3.0 pct up in August.

text.p: Domestic credits in Romania went up by 3.0 percent to 23.6 trillion lei at end-August with government loans rising 9.9 percent after the country had launched its first hard currency bonds, the central bank said.
Two months ago, Romania issued $104.8 million worth of dollar-denominated domestic bonds bearing an annual yield of 7.1 percent and maturing on August 15, 1997.
A central bank report showed credits to government took some 9.0 percent of domestic loans at end-August, when non- government credits grew by 2.4 percent to 21.5 trillion lei.
Hard currency loans continued upwards expanding by 3.2 percent in August from the previous month, the report said.
Medium- and long-term loans accounted for 14.9 percent of end-August leu loans, which stood at 14.23 trillion lei, up from 13.95 trillion in July.
Commercial banks' average leu lending rate for non-bank customers slipped to an annual 55.4 percent in August from 56.8 percent the previous month.
State companies held 57.6 percent of end-August leu loans, almost flat from July's 57.7 percent level.
Inflation was 3.8 percent in August, with the year-on-year rate at 44.2 percent. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
